_comment: THE LINEAGE SCREEN'S REGRESSION FIXTURE for 2002 (kb/Work PB5589): samples of candidate pairs, each read blind and
whole (an Opus reader and a refuter per pair, text only) and labelled SAME, DIFFERENT or DOUBTFUL, each sample with
its expectation. `caught`: the screen's triggers were built from it, and lineage_screen.py --check fails when any of
its DIFFERENT pairs goes unflagged. `known-misses`: the screen was not built from it; --check reports how many of its
DIFFERENT and DOUBTFUL pairs are flagged and fails on none. The fixture pins what the screen catches, never that it
suffices: the second sample is 100 pairs the screen left unflagged, 16 of them not the same requirement. A later
sample is added as a sample of its own, never merged into another.

So the 2002 rule governs identifier-1 in EXIT METHOD RAISING and EXIT FUNCTION RAISING, cases the 2023 rule cannot speak to. The 2023 band is also archaic (F.1). Probe: EXIT FUNCTION compiles clean at --std 2002 and is refused (COBOL0902, removed in 2023) at --std 2023, confirming the 2002-only population. Also depends on exception handling (RAISING), one of 2002's uncatalogued areas.

MERGE general format identical in both editions (USING file-name-2 {file-name-3}..., OUTPUT PROCEDURE/GIVING). The rule is self-contained on record sizes of the SD and the USING files; no referenced rule or enumeration. 2023 changes only neighbouring rules (SR1 placement, key-item restrictions), not this one.

Both formats identical (2023 replaces ROUNDED with rounded-phrase, which does not touch identifier-1/2). Category numeric: 2023 adds new numeric usages (e.g. FLOAT-DECIMAL, BINARY-CHAR etc.) that a 2002 program cannot declare; every 2002 numeric/non-numeric item classifies the same.

Procedure-name-2 appears only in the out-of-line Format 1 THROUGH phrase, identical in both editions. 2023 bands the rule FORMAT 1 (2002 unbanded) which matches where procedure-name-2 occurs. 2023's added Format 3 (exception-checking) and UNTIL EXIT do not involve procedure-name-2.
THROUGH/THRU occurs only in Format 1 (out-of-line) in both editions; 2023 bands the rule FORMAT 1, 2002 leaves it unbanded, which covers the same occurrences. Added Format 3 has no THRU.

REWRITE general format identical (record-name-1 | FILE file-name-1, FROM identifier-1/literal-1, retry, LOCK, INVALID KEY). Renumbered only because 2023 dropped 2002's SR1 (same storage area); this rule itself is unchanged and self-contained.

The 2002 Format 9 and 2023 Format 10 data-pointer-arithmetic formats are identical (SET {identifier-9}... UP|DOWN BY arithmetic-expression-3); format renumbered because 2023 inserted function-pointer-assignment. Companion SR on STRONG restriction also identical.

Set-locale formats identical (2002 Format 10 = 2023 Format 11; same categories and TO operands). The LOCALE clause of SPECIAL-NAMES (LOCALE locale-name-1 IS external-locale-name/literal) exists in both editions.

Format 1 identical in both (index-name-1/identifier-1 TO arithmetic-expression-1/index-name-2/identifier-2); companion SR1-SR3 identical, so the admissible identifier-1 (class index or integer) is the same.
Switch-setting format identical; both leave the set of alterable switches implementor-defined in the same words; no enumeration or referenced rule.
Condition-setting format (TRUE/FALSE) identical; the companion FALSE rule (SR7) identical; conditional variable is the same notion in both.

Object-reference-assignment format identical for identifier-3; 2023 only renames the TO operand class-name-1 to object-class-name-1, which does not touch identifier-3. 2023's new class message-tag is a separate class, so class object admits the same items for 2002 programs.
SORT Format 1 identical in both, with THROUGH/THRU only in INPUT and OUTPUT PROCEDURE phrases; both band the rule FORMAT 1.

2002 already has only STOP RUN [WITH ERROR|NORMAL STATUS [identifier-1|literal-1]] (STOP literal was gone), identical to 2023; literal-1 is the status operand in both. 2023 adds SR4 (no zero-length literal) which concerns a literal kind 2002 lacks.

The 2002 rule is banded FORMATS 1 AND 2: Format 1 (on-overflow, CALL ... USING ... ON OVERFLOW) and Format 2 (on-exception). 2023 has a single Format 1 (Program) with ON EXCEPTION only; Annex E.2 item 1 removes the ON OVERFLOW phrase. The 2002 rule therefore also governs identifier-2 of a CALL ... ON OVERFLOW, a program the 2023 rule does not cover, so the 2023 verdict does not carry for that case. Probe: call-ovf.cob (BY REFERENCE pointer + ON OVERFLOW) is refused with COBOL1679 at --std 2002 (and at 2023 additionally COBOL0882 ON OVERFLOW removed); call-exc.cob refused COBOL1679 at both. So the compiler happens to enforce the 2002-only case, but that is evidence from this probe, not from the 2023 verdict.
All three SUBTRACT formats identical (ROUNDED -> rounded-phrase only); rule banded FORMATS 1 AND 2 in both. Numeric data item: 2023 only adds numeric usages unavailable in 2002.
USE Format 1 (file-exception) identical in both editions; the rule is banded FORMAT 1 in both and concerns only the EXCEPTION|ERROR choice there.

The rule ranges over the enumeration of floating indicators in the clause's table. 2002's table has four entries: *>, >>, the literal continuation indicators, and >>D (floating debugging indicator, obsolete in 2002). 2023's table has only the first three: the debugging indicator was removed (the compiler cites 'removed 2014'). So the 2002 rule also requires >>D to be written on one line, a case the 2023 rule cannot cover. Probe float-d.cob: >>D accepted with obsolete warning COBOL0903 and run (prints OK) at --std 2002; refused COBOL0902 at --std 2023.

The LEADING/TRAILING ==partial-word-1== BY ==partial-word-2== alternative is identical in both formats; the companion rules (one text-word / zero or one text-word, no directive lines) are identical. 2023's removal (E.2) of text-1/literal-3/word-1 operands affects the other REPLACING alternative, not partial-words. The literal kinds named (alphanumeric, boolean, national) exist in both editions.

Format 2 NX literal in both; hexadecimal digits defined identically in both ('0' through '9' and 'A' through 'F', hexadecimal-alphanumeric clause). 2023 makes the sequence optional (zero-length NX"") and raises the length limit, neither of which bears on what characters a sequence may contain.

The rule is a general licence ('whenever literal appears in a format') bounded by item b ('shall not be specified where a syntax rule prohibits it'), so its content is the set of prohibiting syntax rules elsewhere, and that set changed. In 2002 the MOVE rules prohibit only SPACE to numeric/numeric-edited, so SR1 licenses MOVE QUOTE / HIGH-VALUE / LOW-VALUE TO a numeric item (archaic but legal). 2023 MOVE SR5 prohibits every alphanumeric figurative constant to numeric except the digit-only ALL case (Annex E.2 item 1 removal). A 2023-conforming reading of SR1 rejects a program the 2002 rule permits. Probe fig-hv.cob (MOVE QUOTE TO N, N PIC 9(4)): compiles and runs (DONE) at --std 2002; refused COBOL0902 at --std 2023. The compiler gets both right, but through the MOVE edition switch, not the 2023 SR1 verdict. Note this is adjacent to the MOVE figurative behaviour switch the mechanical filter was meant to exclude: the filter missed it because the coupling is through the generic 'a syntax rule' pointer, not a named reference.

Format 6 (ALL literal-1) identical; 2023 SR2 adds 'nor a zero-length literal', a literal kind 2002 lacks. The 2023 MOVE SR5 carve-out (digit-only ALL literal to integer) could be read as reaching multi-digit ALL literals, but the probes show the compiler holds SR3 at both editions: fig-all.cob (MOVE ALL "12" TO N) and fig-cmp.cob (IF N = ALL "12") refused COBOL0902 at --std 2002 and 2023 alike; fig-one.cob (MOVE ALL "7") runs (7777) at both, with an obsolete warning at 2023. The requirement this rule states is the same in both.
General format identical (SELF | [class-name-1 OF] SUPER; 2023 renames class-name-1 to object-class-name-1). All seven syntax rules correspond one to one; 'receiving operand' is the same notion.
Both editions have IS > and IS GREATER THAN. 2023 moves the NOT forms into Format 2 and adds <>, and states NOT > separately (its SR4); the abbreviation '>' for GREATER THAN is unchanged.

Format 2 (prototype) identical; rule under FORMAT 2 in both; same literal-1 note as GR1 (zero-length literal ban is 2023-only and covers nothing 2002 has).

Identical format (INHERITS, USING). 2023 adds SR6/SR7 (no duplicate names in INHERITS/USING) and the zero-length-literal ban; neither touches what the name declares. GR4 renames class-name to object-class-name, a terminology change only.
Format, syntax rules and the three-case enumeration a)-c) identical in both clauses; GR1's reference (9.3.11 Interface implementation) has the same number in both.

The rule quantifies over 'the clauses in the OPTIONS paragraph', and that set is not a subset. 2002's OPTIONS paragraph holds ARITHMETIC (NATIVE | STANDARD) and ENTRY-CONVENTION. 2023's ARITHMETIC clause is NATIVE | STANDARD-BINARY | STANDARD-DECIMAL: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD is gone (2023 also adds DEFAULT ROUNDED, FLOAT-BINARY, FLOAT-DECIMAL, INITIALIZE and INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING). So a 2002 program whose outer program says ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD and whose nested program inherits standard arithmetic through this rule is a case the 2023 rule never governs, because 2023 refuses the clause. The 2023 CONFORMS verdict says nothing about whether contained programs inherit 2002 standard arithmetic. The probe shows the fork: --std 2002 accepts and runs the program, --std 2023 refuses it (COBOL0807). This is cause (b), a clause that lost a form, but reached INDIRECTLY: the rule names no ARITHMETIC phrase, it ranges over the paragraph's clauses. The screen's standard-arithmetic dependency test (keyed on the rule's own words) and its removed-element vocabulary (T6, which lists no ARITHMETIC STANDARD) both miss it. A sixth-cause candidate: a rule quantified over a set of clauses or phrases defined elsewhere ('the clauses in the X paragraph') inherits every change to that set.

property-specifier is PROPERTY property-name-1 [AS literal] in both (literal renumbered literal-5 to literal-4); SR16 identical in substance. 2023 splits the function-specifier into intrinsic and user-defined specifiers, which does not touch property-name-1.

Format identical; GR1-GR6 identical. 2023 adds SR1, which forbids the clause on a file under APPLY COMMIT (a 2023-only feature, so no 2002 program is affected). Format, SR1 and GR1-GR4 identical in both. The clause is an FD clause, so there is no CD reach.
Format and GR1-GR8 identical, including the EC-I-O-LINAGE handling. 2023 adds SR1 (data-names not subject to OCCURS) and drops 'may be qualified'. Neither affects page contiguity.
Format (LIMIT/LIMITS, integer-1 LINES, integer-2 COLUMNS, HEADING/FIRST DETAIL/LAST CH/LAST DE/FOOTING), SR1-SR6 and GR1-GR5 identical.
The three formats are the same with the same integers. 2023 only adds BYTES as a synonym of CHARACTERS (SR2). Rule under ALL FORMATS in both. FD/SD clause, so there is no CD reach.

Rule under FORMAT 2 in both, a)/b) identical. Nearby change noted, not in this rule: GR3 says 'variable-length data item' in 2002 and 'occurs-depending table' in 2023. Cause (a), the communication-section domain, and the screen MISSED it. Likely screen gap: T5 seems to match only clauses NAMED in the 13.14 format (its '-clause' meta-terms); the inline keyword clauses of 13.14.1 format 1 (SIGN, SYNCHRONIZED, JUSTIFIED, BLANK WHEN ZERO, ANY LENGTH, BASED, PROPERTY, SAME AS, TYPE, ALIGNED, GROUP-USAGE, REDEFINES, TYPEDEF, EXTERNAL, GLOBAL, DESTINATION/INVALID/PRESENT WHEN/VARYING) need the same treatment. This hypothesis comes from reading plan-2002/PLAN-2002-v3-K0.md T5, not from the screen's code. The compiler is right on the CD case: the probe at --std 2002 shows a SIGN LEADING SYNC item in a CD record with its sign on the leading digit (digit image '}12' for -12), the same as the working-storage twin.

SR1 identical (same containers: function, program, factory, instance; not method or interface). 2023 adds type-declaration entries to the format and an extra initialization reference (OPTIONS INITIALIZE clause) in GR3; neither changes which data is static.
selection-subject, selection-object and range-expression formats identical (literal-1..4, partial-expression, IN alphabet-name). GR3a-f identical.

'As detailed below' points at GR4-GR6, which are identical in both editions (report heading, page heading, control headings, then detail; then control footings and headings; the page-advance steps a-f). Only the clause numbers in the cross-references are renumbered (TYPE, NEXT GROUP, CONTROL). GR7 differs ('if it is enabled' in 2023), but GR7 is not this rule.

Format 2 (historic) with NEXT SENTENCE is present in both and archaic in both (the 2002 NOTE and 2023 F.1). SR3 (ELSE NEXT SENTENCE may be omitted) is identical. 2023 only restructures SR2's matching text.
The same FORMAT 2 band and GR3-GR7 set in both editions.

The ALLOCATE format and SR1-SR5 are identical. The rule works by reference to the INITIALIZE statement, and that text DID change, so this was checked closely. (1) 2023 adds function-pointer and message-tag categories (widening). (2) The real change: in 2002 GR5c1b any table-format VALUE clause makes every occurrence a VALUE-phrase receiver. In 2023 GR5c1c only an occurrence that the VALUE clause gives a value counts. For an occurrence a 2002 FROM ... TO table VALUE leaves out, 2002 qualifies it under VALUE (so TO DEFAULT never applies) but GR6a3 supplies no literal, and VALUE GR4 leaves such data undefined. 2023 sends the category default. So 2023 resolves a case 2002 leaves undefined, and 2023 conformance stays inside 2002's latitude. The probe agrees: both editions print '[  AABB  07ZZ]' (occurrences 1 and 4 set to spaces). Flagged as a referenced-by-name change the screen did not catch; the result is SAME only because 2002's side is undefined.

Format identical (record-name-1 | FILE file-name-1, FROM identifier-1 | literal-1, retry, LOCK, INVALID KEY). 2023 drops 2002 SR1 (record-name-1 and identifier-1 not the same storage) in favor of a NOTE on overlap, and adds SR5 (APPLY COMMIT, 2023-only). The connector identification is unchanged.
Under the band 'RELATIVE AND INDEXED FILES' in both editions; same operands (identifier-1, literal-1, record-name-1). The line-sequential rules 2023 adds sit in the sequential band before it.

Format 7 (data-pointer-assignment) is the same diagram in both, and FORMAT 7 SR17-SR19 are identical. The rule sits under FORMAT 7 in both. 2023 renumbers later formats (function-pointer), which does not touch format 7.

Both formats (file, table) identical, with the KEY phrase repeatable in both; rule under ALL FORMATS in both. 2023 SR3 turns into a syntax refusal the format-1 SORT inside an input or output procedure that 2002 rejects at run time (EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE, results undefined). That removes no 2002 case where key direction has a defined outcome. Key data-name restrictions are reworded (2023 adds dynamic-length and message-tag exclusions); the 2002 keys are unchanged.

The referenced OCCURS rules for 2002's tables are identical: fixed GR4 and variable/occurs-depending GR7-GR8, with the same EC-BOUND-ODO and the same sending/receiving extent. 2023 renames 'variable-length data item' to 'occurs-depending group item' and adds format 4 (dynamic-capacity), a widening. The data-name-2 subscripting moves from 2002 SR13 (rightmost subscript ALL for multi-level tables) to 2023 SR13 and 8.4.2.3 SR5e/SR6, which still admit rightmost ALL and also allow omitting it, so every 2002 form is kept.

Format 2 (table SORT) is the same in both: SORT data-name-2 [ON ASCENDING/DESCENDING KEY [data-name-1]...]. The neighbouring format-2 general rules (2002 GR17-23 = 2023 GR18-24) are word-identical, renumbered by one because 2023 inserted a file-control cross-reference GR6 in format 1. The key-data-item syntax rules changed only by 2023 restrictions on 2023-only things (dynamic-length items, message-tag, variable-length groups) and 'key data names shall not be subscripted'; data-name-2 subscripting moved from 'rightmost subscript ALL' to 'in accordance with Subscripts', which does not touch which KEY phrase governs the order. The override rule reaches no 2002-only form.

General format of START is identical in both editions (FIRST / KEY relational-operator data-name-1|record-key-name-1 [WITH LENGTH] / LAST, INVALID KEY phrases). The only syntax change is 2023 SR4 (keys not subject to OCCURS) replacing 2002 SR4 (qualification), which does not touch GR2. The RECORD clause DEPENDING ON phrase exists in both. No 2002-only form reached.

Same format and same file organizations (relative, indexed, sequential sections GR8-21 word-identical apart from 2023 GR17e adding SUPPRESS WHEN, a 2023-only phrase). The unsuccessful-START outcome rule reaches no 2002-only form.

STRING format identical; identifier-4 SR (2002 SR6 = 2023 SR7) word-identical. 2023 adds restrictions only on 2023-only things (zero-length literal-2, variable-length group, dynamic-length items). The POINTER precondition reaches no 2002-only form.
Format and GR1-3 identical. 2023 adds SR2 excluding files named in APPLY COMMIT; APPLY COMMIT does not exist in 2002, so no 2002 program is excluded. The rule reaches no 2002-only form.

Cause (b), missed by the screen: the COPY clause lost forms in 2023. 'The replacing action of a COPY statement' in 2002 covers the REPLACING operands text-1 BY text-2 (identifiers, archaic), word-1 BY word-2 and literal-3 BY literal-4, and pseudo-text that may contain debugging lines; the 2023 format and GR8 keep only pseudo-text and partial-word, and 2023 has no debugging lines. Conformance to the 2023 rule says nothing about the replacing action of a 2002 COPY ... REPLACING W BY V. (For those forms the restriction is largely satisfied by 2002 SR9/SR10, but that is a further 2002-only argument, not something the 2023 verdict shows.) Probe: copyword.cob compiles and runs at --std 2002 (prints AAA) and is rejected at --std 2023 with COBOL0902 'a non-pseudo-text COPY REPLACING operand (identifier/literal/word) was removed in COBOL-2023'.

Cause (b) variant, missed by the screen: what pseudo-text-1 admits changed. In 2002 pseudo-text-1 and pseudo-text-2 may contain debugging lines (SR10), whose text-words participate in matching (GR8c6) and whose replacement stays on a debugging line (GR11); 2023 has no debugging lines (SR10, GR8c6 and GR11 are gone, and the transcription has no occurrence of 'debugging line'). So GR2 in 2002 governs a REPLACE whose pseudo-text-1 spans a debugging line; the 2023 rule cannot. Probe: replacedbg.cob at --std 2002 compiles with obsolete warnings and prints REP / ABC (the two DISPLAYs, one on a D line, matched as one pseudo-text-1); at --std 2023 it is rejected, COBOL0902 'the fixed-form debugging line (indicator D) was removed'. The REPLACE format itself is unchanged.

Both formats (B"..." and BX"...") exist in both editions with the same separators. 2023 widens: zero-length literals and up to 8,191 positions (2002: 1 to 160). Every 2002 boolean literal is a 2023 boolean literal with the same separators.
Format 2 (hexadecimal-boolean) and its SR3 'Hexadecimal-digit-1 shall be a hexadecimal digit' are the same in both; the digit-to-bit table is identical. 2023 only adds the zero-length case (GR7).

End-marker format has the same nine alternatives (2023 renames class-name-1 to object-class-name-1, which SR3 does not touch). Nested-program END PROGRAM ordering rule reaches no 2002-only form.

INTERFACE-ID format identical. The referenced REPOSITORY class-specifier and interface-specifier (2002 12.2.7.1, 2023 12.3.8.2) have the same shape (CLASS name [AS] [EXPANDS ... USING ...], INTERFACE name [AS] [EXPANDS ... USING ...]); 2023 only renames class-name to object-class-name. 2023 adds SR6/SR7 (no duplicate names), restrictions with no bearing on SR4.
OBJECT-COMPUTER format (CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION locale-phrase-1/2, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE) and all its rules are word-identical; the SPECIAL-NAMES LOCALE clause has the same form in both.
THROUGH/THRU appear in the same two places in both formats (the ALPHABET literal-phrase and the CLASS clause). 2023's new dynamic-length-structure clause has no THROUGH.

The alphabet-name-clause is identical in both (alphanumeric: LOCALE/NATIVE/STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2/code-name-1/literal-phrase; national: LOCALE/NATIVE/UCS-4/UTF-8/UTF-16/code-name-2/literal-phrase). Same implementor-defined item.

Both formats are 'SPECIAL-NAMES.' followed by optional clauses and a closing period; with no clause, 'SPECIAL-NAMES. .' may drop one period in both. The clause list differs only by 2023's additional dynamic-length-structure clause (and clause order), which does not change the empty case.
Exclusive list of four clauses, each with the same form in both editions; all other 2002 clauses are barred in an interface definition in both.

switch-name-1 IS mnemonic-name-1 has the same form in both. SR5 is unaffected.

Clause format (STANDARD-1 | feature-name-1) identical and in file-control format 3 in both. The STANDARD-1 general rules changed (2002 'magnetic tape file', ISO 1001:1986 7.2; 2023 'tape drive', ISO/IEC 1001:2012 7.1.2) but SR2 concerns only feature-name-1, an implementor-defined list in both.

The ASSIGN clause (TO device-name-1|literal-1 ... [USING data-name-1] | USING data-name-1) is identical in all four formats in both editions; implementor-defined in both. 2023 SR4 bars a zero-length literal-1 (2023-only). Both formats of the clause and all GRs identical; the referenced ALTERNATE RECORD KEY and RECORD KEY clauses have the same data-name forms (2023 adds SUPPRESS WHEN, a widening). 2023 adds SR6 'shall not be subscripted', which restates what a data-name already implies in both.
Three formats identical; SR2-10 and the format-3 GRs identical. 2023 adds SR11/GR3 for APPLY COMMIT files (2023-only), which do not touch the SORT/SORT-MERGE equivalence.

Three formats identical (file-area, record-area, sort-merge-area), SR1-SR10 identical in both editions; 2023 adds only SR11 and GR3 (APPLY COMMIT sharing), a 2023-only restriction that does not touch SR3. A permission over the organizations and access modes; both editions have sequential, relative and indexed organization and sequential/random/dynamic access, and report and sort-merge files. 2023 SR11 (APPLY COMMIT) adds an unrelated restriction. Same clause text otherwise.
General format identical; the clause's only syntax rule; GR1-GR4 identical. BLOCK CONTAINS is an FD/SD clause in both, no CD reach.

Both formats (report-writer, screen-item) identical, the ALL FORMATS band identical, SR1-SR13 and GR1-GR19 identical apart from renumbered cross-references (13.16.37 -> 13.18.39 PAGE) and NOTE wording. Report and screen sections exist in both editions.

FORMAT 1 band in both; format 1 identical (LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT, integer-1 absolute, PLUS integer-2 relative); GR6 (absolute placement by LEFT/RIGHT/CENTER) identical. Default LEFT stated in the rule itself in both.
